questions.q: What is the first step when creating a new customer in Receivables?
options: Search the shared party registry to avoid creating a duplicate party
questions.explain: Because parties are shared across Oracle Fusion applications, the party may already exist from a Sales or Service interaction, so searching first avoids duplicates.

questions.q: What is the absolute minimum needed before a new customer can be billed?
options: A customer account, at least one account site, and a Bill-To use on that site
A completed credit check and three references
questions.explain: A party alone cannot be billed. Receivables requires a customer account with an account site carrying a Bill-To use at minimum.

questions.q: In the Cascade Outdoor Supply example, why did the AR specialist search the party registry before creating anything?
options: Because Cascade had already transacted with Northwind years earlier
Because new parties are not allowed in Oracle Fusion
To check whether the party already existed anywhere in the shared registry, even though in this case it didn't
questions.explain: The search is a standard first step regardless of outcome — in this example it confirmed Cascade was genuinely new, so a new party was created.

questions.q: Which of these can be added to a customer record AFTER the first invoice is already billable?
questions.explain: Contacts and bank accounts round out the record but are not required before billing can begin; they can be added at any time afterward.

questions.q: What site use, besides Bill-To, is typically assigned alongside it during customer creation?
questions.explain: Ship-To is the other common site use, identifying where goods are delivered; it supports fulfillment and tax determination.
